title: Predict gating where the done cannot yet be run
description:
The classifier half, and the reason gvc is not purely mechanical (operator, 2026-09-22: 'are there still scenarios where an llm classifier is useful... i would imagine yes').

Running the done is an oracle only for items runnable NOW. The case that defeats it is not exotic - it is the ordinary one, and this session produced the exemplar. qu3's finding says: 'when s45 wires the table's value into a cloud dispatch, a value routed into a container boot will be refused', and then says why no test caught it: 'no test boots a container'. Nothing was red. The finding IS a prediction, and deciding whether it gates the done is reasoning about prose against prose.

THE QUESTION, which is Jev-shaped on purpose: a Choice over THIS EPIC'S OWN ACCEPTANCE
ITEMS plus 'none', with confidence. A closed enum per epic is Jev's sweet spot, and the
answer doubles as the item id that absorption has to name. Reuse the classifier wne's
0ju built rather than starting a second one.

ERR TOWARD ABSORBING, and put the reasoning in the code where someone will later be
tempted to tune it the other way: a false positive costs the epic work it did not need;
a false negative closes an epic whose goal is unmet, in a factory where nobody is
watching. Those are not the same cost. The threshold sits on the cheap side.

The verdict is recorded as PREDICTED, never as observed. A retro that cannot tell a
guess from a measurement cannot report honestly, and the next tick scores predictions
against what the done later did - which is impossible if the two are indistinguishable.
acceptance_criteria: A finding whose relevant acceptance items are not yet runnable is classified against the epic's own items plus 'none', with confidence, reusing the existing Jev client; the verdict is recorded as PREDICTED and is distinguishable from an OBSERVED one in the record; the threshold is documented as deliberately biased toward absorbing with the cost asymmetry stated; an unreachable classifier falls back to absorbing rather than to deferring; and go test -short ./... passes
